house.description: Administrative hearings provisions amended for human rights cases.

House.text: Introduction and first reading, referred to Judiciary Finance and Civil Law

bill_text.text_with_changes:
A bill for an act relating to human rights; amending administrative hearings provision for human rights cases; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 363A.29, subdivision 1.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 363A.29, subdivision 1, is amended to read:

Subdivision 1.
Conduct of hearings.
A determination issued by the commissioner may be heard as a contested case[-, except that-][+.+] The report of the administrative law judge shall be binding on all parties to the proceeding and if appropriate shall be implemented by an order as provided for in subdivision 3. The party contesting the determination issued by the commissioner may file a request with the commissioner to appear at a hearing on the party's own behalf or through a private attorney. The commissioner shall [+decide within 30 days whether to +]forward the request for hearing to the [-Office-][+ Court+] of Administrative Hearings, which shall promptly set the matter for hearing. [-The hearing shall be conducted at a place designated by the commissioner, within the county where the unfair discriminatory practice occurred or where the respondent resides or has a principal place of business.-] The hearing shall be conducted in accordance with sections 14.57 to 14.62, and is subject to appeal in accordance with sections 14.63 to 14.68.
bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to human rights; amending administrative hearings provision for human rights cases; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 363A.29, subdivision 1.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 363A.29, subdivision 1, is amended to read:

Subdivision 1.
Conduct of hearings.
A determination issued by the commissioner may be heard as a contested case. The report of the administrative law judge shall be binding on all parties to the proceeding and if appropriate shall be implemented by an order as provided for in subdivision 3. The party contesting the determination issued by the commissioner may file a request with the commissioner to appear at a hearing on the party's own behalf or through a private attorney. The commissioner shall decide within 30 days whether to forward the request for hearing to the Court of Administrative Hearings, which shall promptly set the matter for hearing. The hearing shall be conducted in accordance with sections 14.57 to 14.62, and is subject to appeal in accordance with sections 14.63 to 14.68.
deletions: The hearing shall be conducted at a place designated by the commissioner, within the county where the unfair discriminatory practice occurred or where the respondent resides or has a principal place of business.
